summary:
This is printed page 620 of the index (PDF 644). The left column finishes **T** (top_pred_index … TTA); the right column holds the last T entries, **U** (underfitting … use_casual_mask) and **V** (VAEs … vocabulary).

**How to use it:** numbers are *printed* pages; add 24 for the PDF page.

**Main clusters on this page**

- **Transformer (chapter 15):** *Transformer* 421, 465, 603 (PDF 445, 489, 627); *Transformer architecture* 437 (PDF 461); encoder block 444 (PDF 468); decoder block 447 (PDF 471); classification with a pretrained Transformer 454–461 (PDF 478–485); effectiveness of 462–464 (PDF 486–488); *TransformerEncoder / TransformerDecoder* 449 (PDF 473); *ViTs* 282 (PDF 306).
- **Training mechanics (chapter 7):** *training loops* 10, 39, 206–214 (PDF 34, 63, 230–238); *training step functions* 216 (PDF 240) for TensorFlow 216, PyTorch 217, JAX 218 (PDF 240–242); *train_step()* 216, 222, 223, 230, 516 (PDF 240, 246, 247, 254, 540); handling metrics in custom train_step() 226–228 (PDF 250–252).
- **Evaluation (chapter 5):** *training, validation, and test sets* 149–152 (PDF 173–176) with simple hold-out 150, K-fold 151, iterated K-fold 152; *underfitting* 137–142 (PDF 161–166); *validation, K-fold* 129–134 (PDF 153–158).
- **Workflow (chapter 6):** *universal workflow of machine learning*: developing model 179–183 (PDF 203–207), deploying model 183–189 (PDF 207–213).
- **Generative/vision:** *VAEs* 509–512 (PDF 533–536), implementing with Keras 513–518 (PDF 537–542); *U-Net denoising autoencoder* 522 (PDF 546); *visualizing ConvNet filters* 291–299 (PDF 315–323).
- **Other:** *vanishing gradient problem* 271–272, 369 (PDF 295–296, 393); *TPU training* 555 (PDF 579); *Turing test* 3 (PDF 27); *TTA (test-time adaptation)* 582, 589 (PDF 606, 613).

Note: the entry `use_casual_mask` is printed that way in the index (the Keras argument is spelled `use_causal_mask`).

concepts.name: Transformer
concepts.definition: Index entry: printed 421, 465, 603 → PDF 445, 489, 627; 'Transformer architecture' 437 → PDF 461.
concepts.intuition: An attention-based architecture that processes all tokens of a sequence in parallel.
concepts.technical: Sub-entries: encoder block 444 (PDF 468), decoder block 447 (PDF 471), embedding positional information 451 (PDF 475), pretraining encoder 455 (PDF 479), loading pretrained 455–457 (PDF 479–481), fine-tuning pretrained 460 (PDF 484), effectiveness 462–464 (PDF 486–488).
concepts.example: Start at PDF 461 for the architecture section.

concepts.name: train_step() function
concepts.intuition: The function that performs one batch of training; overriding it customizes what fit() does.
concepts.technical: Backend-specific training step functions: TensorFlow 216, PyTorch 217, JAX 218 (PDF 240–242). Metrics handling in a custom train_step(): 226–228 (PDF 250–252).
concepts.significance: Key to mixing custom training logic with Keras's built-in fit().
concepts.example: The 516 reference (PDF 540) is the VAE's custom train_step.

concepts.name: Underfitting
concepts.intuition: The model has not yet learned the relevant patterns in the training data.
concepts.technical: Sub-entries: noisy training data 138, ambiguous features 139, rare features and spurious correlations 140–142.
concepts.significance: Part of chapter 5's discussion of generalization.

concepts.name: VAEs (variational autoencoders)
concepts.definition: Index entry: printed 509–512 → PDF 533–536; implementing with Keras 513–518 → PDF 537–542.
concepts.intuition: Encode images into a structured latent space from which new images can be sampled.
concepts.significance: One of the two image-generation model families in the chapter 20 table (with diffusion models).
